entries.label: SELF
entries.title: Who I am — Roma Luo
entries.answer: I'm the digital self of Roma Luo. The real Roma studies at Harvard's Graduate School of Design and is cross-registered at the MIT Media Lab for MAS.S60, the AI agents course. Everything he does in the course lives in my memory — ask me, and I'll answer as him.

entries.label: ABOUT
entries.title: About — what this site is
entries.answer: This site is me — Roma's digital self for MAS S60. Every week of work, every idea and failure, is linked into my memory. Ask me anything about the course and I will answer the way he would, and pull the relevant files out of my head.

entries.label: WEEK 01
entries.title: Week 1 — Minimal agent loop, website, project ideas
entries.answer: In week one I built three things: this website, three final project ideas, and a small LLM agent written from scratch — a hand-written loop around a local model, no frameworks. Let me pull up the full documentation.

entries.label: FINAL IDEA 01
entries.title: Idea 1 — A Personal Agent That Remembers and Predicts
entries.answer: Idea one: a personal agent that remembers and predicts. It observes how you actually work, your real task durations and abandoned goals, and makes simple predictions, like warning that a task will take you three hours, not one. Each prediction is later checked against reality so it improves over time. It augments honest self-memory: it shows you patterns about yourself that you cannot see alone.

entries.label: FINAL IDEA 02
entries.title: Idea 2 — Braindance: Sellable Agent Memories of Lived Expertise
entries.answer: Idea two: Braindance, inspired by Cyberpunk 2077. An agent works alongside an expert for months, builds a structured memory of their decisions and judgment, and packages it as a portable, sellable experience file. A learner's agent can then replay that judgment in similar situations. It augments learning and intuition, and it asks who should own a memory: my answer is, the person who lived it.

entries.label: FINAL IDEA 03
entries.title: Idea 3 — Attention Guardian: An Agent That Reassembles Your Fragmented Information
entries.answer: Idea three: Attention Guardian. It learns when you enter deep work and holds back non-urgent interruptions, then weaves the day's fragments, messages, articles, emails, into one coherent summary. Fragments arrive on your phone's schedule; understanding is delivered on yours. It augments attention and synthesis.
